frase_gancho.texto: Children of the milpa and the jungle who preserve time and ancestral knowledge.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Step into the diverse universe of the contemporary Maya peoples, whose lands stretch from the Yucatán Peninsula to the highlands of Chiapas. This gallery shows how the Tzotzil, Tzeltal, Tojolabal, Chontal, and peninsular Maya sustain a living cosmological continuity. Visitors will see replicas of traditional housing architecture built of bajareque and palm thatch, the textile richness of brocaded huipiles, and woolen garments made for the cold of the mountains. The exhibition emphasizes devotion to the sacred milpa, the prayers of the Cha-Chaac ritual to bring rain, and the linguistic and cultural resistance of this people.
